title: Sitting in around Los Angeles as a newcomer
summary: Howard says he went to clubs and Lee Larkins's place trying to sit in, sometimes being told to leave, until he proved himself.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Can I ask a couple more things? A last couple of questions?
A last couple, then we're getting ready to wind up anyway, but we're so close, we really are, and then you're going to have a chance to really relax.
Yeah.

We were talking before about when you got to Los Angeles, and I just wondered if there were any more places you remember about, because you said that when you first got here, to get acquainted with people in music you just went and played where the music was and one of the places was at Lee Larkin's house, where there was a band playing, musicians hung around, Lee Larkin sold whiskey and he was pretty popular, but that probably wasn't the only place. Do you remember where else, when you were just getting into music here in Los Angeles, do you remember where else you went to play, to sit in?
No, I don't. I can't remember, not another place.
What went on? Were there jam sessions then or was that something that came later?
That's something that came later. That came later.
So if you wanted to sit in you'd what, go to a dance or go to where somebody was rehearsing, or just playing for their own enjoyment, or --
Well, I'd go to one of them places where a band was playing.
Like a club?
At a club or someplace, and try to get to sit down and play.
I see.
If they'd let me. Lots of times they'd tell me, "Get the hell out of here."
(Laughter)
Lee Larkins, he was a guy that owned a place, he'd say, "We don't want you in there with that noise."
(Laughter)
But you apparently stuck it out till you were accepted, is that right?
Well, they didn't say nothing about it. They tried to help me all they could. And even they were -- they were Christian gentlemen.
Could you hold the mike up?
Yeah. They were Christian gentlemen. That's the only thing I can say about them. And my aunt died the other day, not long ago. There I go again. She knew. She knew those people very well.
So apparently it wasn't very long before the people in Los Angeles, the musicians here, knew that they had a good player, that somebody new had come to town that was very good.
Yeah.
Because you just persistently kept showing up with your horn to show them that you could play.
Yeah.
Is that right?
Yeah, that's right. Kept on at it, showed that I could play. Now I'm going to quit.
All right. Thank you.
Excuse me.
Okay.
